title: Clavicula Salomonis and Septem sigilla planetarum in a secret alphabet, Basel UB, UBH AN V 9 (17th century): key recovered from the volume's own clear copy, three held-out passages decoded, not read (contributed by Malcolm McBratney with Claude)

documents.shelfmark: Basel, Universitätsbibliothek, UBH AN V 9 (old shelfmark K IV 19), the cipher leaves transcribed here: ff. 4r and 4v (training), 15r lines 1-12 (H1), 159r (H2), 34r rims of pentacles 3 and 4 (H3); e-manuscripta.ch, https://doi.org/10.7891/e-manuscripta-185551

plaintext.source: The volume's own clear copy: ff. 101r-155r give the text of ff. 3r-96v and ff. 166r-170r that of ff. 158r-162r, 'aber in normaler Schrift geschrieben' (Steinmann's unprinted description, PRIOR_ART.md). The held-out passages' counterparts are ff. 109v (H1), 167r (H2) and 123r (H3). The volume also holds its key: f. 99r (Danish notes) with a German translation on f. 98r, viewed here only after the decode.

transcription.source: e-manuscripta IIIF page images 2000 px wide (https://www.e-manuscripta.ch/i3f/v20/<page id>/full/2000,/0/default.jpg, FETCH_LOG.txt), with zoomed crops; the pentacle rims from a polar unwrap (scripts/unwrap.py)
transcription.notes: Length: _check_profile.py --measure transcription.txt --drop-first gives 2634 whitespace tokens = 2132 signs + 475 word separators (/) + 12 line fillers (Fill) + 15 line-end hyphens (Eq); distinct 99 = 96 sign labels with their marks + /, Fill and Eq. By page: f. 4r 546 signs, f. 4v 681, f. 15r lines 1-12 290, f. 159r 563, f. 34r rims 52. With the dot above, the dot below and the diaeresis split off as tokens of their own (scripts/common.py): training 1,383 key tokens, held-out 1,034 (work/decode_counts.txt). One reader (Claude Opus 5.5), one pass; the training leaves were transcribed with the clear copy beside them and the held-out leaves by a reader who already knew most of the system (FREEZE_TX.txt). 8 signs not identified (?), 1 in training and 7 held out. Frozen before any key building (FREEZE_TX.txt). Not checked by a person.

system.summary: A secret alphabet of invented and digit-like signs for Latin letters, with signs for common letter groups (et, er, es, it, st, ct, sc, nt, ae), a few word signs (qui, quod, quam, que, non), and marks on a sign that add m (dot above) or n (dot below) or double its letter (two dots above).

diacritics.note: A dot above a sign adds m and a dot below adds n after its letter; two dots above double the letter; two dots on the line repeat a vowel written earlier in the word (the key leaf: the letter before with a dot in its middle) and three dots a letter further back; a bar or a loop on a sign makes another sign (Bx~ non, Oe~, Tk@, Dl@).

system.notes: 51 base sign labels (SIGNS.md, the placeholder ? not counted) and 6 marks; the recovered key (KEY.tsv) values 62 tokens and two rules. Homophones counted from KEY.tsv: e has 6, D1 and Cd, s has 6s, 6v, Ph and Ar; several of these are word-final forms or context signs on the key leaf (Ea a, Lr t, Pl r and Ar s final; D1 e after r, i after t). The 7 word signs met in training are Oe" quod, Oe^m quam, Oei qui, Oe~ (quas or quae in training, quem on the leaf), Q3 que, Bx~ non and 5~ (igitur, no letters in the key); the key leaf lists more (quae, enim, autem) and calls them abbreviations as usual in Latin. Line fillers and line-end hyphens carry no value. The volume's own key leaf (f. 99r, Danish; German translation f. 98r) is the same key; it was compared only after the decode (work/keyleaf_vs_key.tsv).

prior_solution.where: In the volume itself: the clear copy (ff. 101r-155r, 166r-170r) and the key leaf f. 99r with its German translation f. 98r (Steinmann's description; swisscollections). No edition, study or published decipherment of the cipher found in Cyphersolver's issues and repository, DECODE, the web or Schmeh's list of encrypted books (PRIOR_ART.md). Not opened: Skinner and Rankine 2008, Mathers 1889, Boudet's census of Clavicula manuscripts.

conditions.human_role: Malcolm McBratney directed the work and set its rules (prior art first; the adjacent-plaintext track; the key leaves kept unseen until the key was frozen; transcription and key frozen before one decode; held-out passages; a separate strict judge; the first pass as the figure of record; shuffle controls), and the swisscollections record was read in his own Chrome session after he cleared its bot check. Claude sessions did the transcription, key recovery, decode, judging, reading and translation. No person has read the signs or the text without AI.

scripts/unwrap.py: polar unwrap of the pentacle rims for transcription
pass3/scripts/decode_p3.py and run_decode.py: the pass 3 decoder (rules C1-C5) and its one run with the frozen hashes asserted
pass3/scripts/control_p3.py: 5,000 shuffled keys at two seeds, own Latin letter 4-gram model
pass3/scripts/score_p3.py: the solver's own strict count and the clear-copy match for H1
pass3/variant/make_variant.py, run_variant.py, score_variant.py: the declared decode without C4 and C5 and its score

solution.what: Prior art before any transcription (11:59-12:10 UTC): Cyphersolver issues and issue bodies, the repository (catalogue, leads, COVERAGE), DECODE public search, web searches, Schmeh's list of encrypted books, Steinmann's unprinted description (UB Basel PDF) and the swisscollections record (PRIOR_ART.md). No reading, edition or study of the cipher found; the catalogue names the clear copy and the key leaves.

IIIF manifest 5353221 (380 canvases) and page images at 2000 px by plain curl (FETCH_LOG.txt). The e-manuscripta title page and swisscollections showed bot checks to curl, not passed by the script; swisscollections was read in the contributor's own browser. The key leaves ff. 98-99 (canvases 199-206) were quarantined in scripts/fetch.sh until the key was frozen.

Split recorded before any key building (SPLIT.md): training ff. 4r-4v against the clear ff. 101r-102r; held out H1 f. 15r lines 1-12, H2 f. 159r, H3 f. 34r rims of pentacles 3 and 4. Transcribed by sign shape with neutral labels (SIGNS.md): 2,132 signs, 51 base labels, 8 signs not identified. Frozen at 12:51:30 UTC (FREEZE_TX.txt). The training leaves were transcribed with the clear copy beside them.

Run 1 (scripts/solve.py, training files only): word alignment of cipher to clear words and an EM emission model, 300 word pairs. Two modelling faults found on the training data: the dots above the oe-sign split off as a doubling mark (giving quo + d for quod), and one-sign words of four letters (quam, quae) unable to align (work/KEY_run1.tsv, SOLVE_LOG.md).

Run 2, the key of record: 301 word pairs, no cipher word unpaired, 62 tokens valued. Two context rules adopted on training counts (bar 70%): two dots on the line = the nearest preceding vowel of the word (34 of 43), two dots above = the letter twice (14 of 14). Ambiguous tokens take their majority value (Cl r 9 / i 6; Dl@ s 9 / us 8 / as 7). Key frozen at 12:55:46 UTC (FREEZE_KEY.txt).

One decode of the three held-out passages with the frozen key (scripts/decode_once.py, DECODE.txt): 1,034 key tokens, 10 with no key value, 1,138 letters; no emendation. The placeholder label ? (sign not identified) carries the value i from its one training use, so the 7 unidentified held-out signs decode as i.

Separate strict judge (Claude Opus 5.5, given only judge/BRIEF.txt and judge/decode.txt) scored each letter S (in a word that reads as sense), E (one-letter slip) or N: H1 229/367 = 62.4% (below the contributor's 65% line), H2 470/702 = 67.0%, H3 48/69 = 69.6%, all 747/1,138 = 65.6% (judge/judge.tsv, re-added by judge/count.py; the lenient count, for sensitivity only, gives 73.6%).

After the decode the clear counterparts were located and transcribed: f. 109v (H1), 167r (H2) and 123r (H3, against SPLIT.md's expectation that the pentacles had none). Clear letters reproduced (Levenshtein, abbreviations expanded): H1 311/425 = 73.2%, H2 616/733 = 84.0%, H3 61/73 = 83.6%, all 988/1,231 = 80.3% (score/score_clear_out.txt). Identical words in order: 43.4%, 42.8%, 57.1% (score/worddiff_out.txt).

Shuffle control: the key's values permuted among its 58 base tokens (the three mark tokens and the two-dot rule fixed), 5,000 keys at each of seeds 20261112 and 7, scored with the la-letters model (lang/) and by clear-copy match: 0 of 5,000 reach the real key on any statistic, z 5.2 to 7.2 for the model and 10.6 to 14.1 for the clear match (score/shuffle_out.txt).

The volume's key leaf f. 99r (Danish) was viewed only after the key freeze and the decode and transcribed with this project's labels (tx/KEYLEAF_f099r.txt). Of the 52 recovered values it covers, 46 agree; 4 differ (Dl@ s where the leaf has us, Oe~ quas for quem, Lmt an for at, D3 o where the leaf has a positional rule); Cl depends on context on the leaf; the two-dot rule is an approximation of the leaf's. 10 recovered tokens are not on the leaf (work/keyleaf_vs_key.tsv).

Lexicon check, not the judge: the share of decoded letters in words of the shared Latin lexicon is H1 30.8%, H2 44.0%, H3 36.2%, against 79.8%, 77.1% and 54.8% for the clear copy (score/lexcheck_out.txt). In-sample fit on the training leaves: 92.8% of clear letters reproduced (score/train_fit_out.txt).

reading.md and translation.md made by the assembling session from DECODE.txt and the judge's word tags, nothing emended: words read as sense H1 35/77 (0.455), H2 70/133 (0.526), H3 8/15 (0.533), all 113/225 (0.502); docs/_check_reading.py finds no clean sentence (H1 0/7, H2 0/11, H3 0/2). All three passages filed 'decoded, not read', the target 'not read'. A decoder written here from KEY.tsv and the transcriptions reproduces DECODE.txt on 37 of 37 lines (validation.tsv).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1024 tokens, 49 types, la order 4: reading -2.639 per letter; random keys -4.459 (z 5.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.782 (mean -2.817, z 6.5); annealer on the real text -2.553. Verdict: pass.
Pass 2 (keyleaf/): key leaf ff. 98r-99r, pentacle pages ff. 33r-54r, f. 97r-v and clear f. 123r-v fetched at full size by plain IIIF GET, 37 images, all HTTP 200 (keyleaf/IMAGE_FETCH.tsv).

keyleaf/KEY_LEAF.tsv transcribed from the volume's own key leaf f. 99r (Danish; German f. 98r) only: 73 sign values, 5 pairs, 2 whole-word forms, 6 rules; the two-dot rule refers back to the letter drawn with a dot in its middle.

The 8 first-pass ? signs looked at on the full-size images after the first decode (not blind): 7 labelled (6; 4" and Xco_ with an unrecorded 6^, X Ea read as Xz; X Hkf; Hkf; Ab; 4~), 1 still unidentified (f. 4r l. 17). Changes only in keyleaf/tx2/ (CHANGES.tsv); first pass unchanged.

First-series pentacle rims nos. 11-110 (ff. 35r-51r) unwrapped from full-size images and transcribed by shape: 62 rims with a cipher inscription, 38 blank, crosses only or in ordinary script (keyleaf/tx/PENTACLES.txt). Not blind: the transcriber knew the key leaf. Second series ff. 52r-54r and f. 97r-v not transcribed.
Freeze keyleaf/FREEZE_PENT.txt 03:33:21 UTC, RFC 3161 stamps Sectigo and FreeTSA, committed and pushed (b8cce3928) before any decode of the new text.

One decode with the key leaf (keyleaf/scripts/decode_keyleaf.py; declared fallback for the two-dot sign where no inner dot was recorded): training 1,556 letters, H1 382, H2 717, H3 69, pentacles 2,520 (keyleaf/DECODE_KEYLEAF.txt). No emendation.

Shuffle control, key-leaf values permuted among 73 signs, 5,000 keys at seeds 20261112 and 7, la-letters: every section and all 62 pentacles 0/5000 at both seeds; pentacles z 10.5 / 10.3, lowest single rim z 4.1 (keyleaf/work/shuffle_keyleaf_out.txt).

Separate judge for pass 2 could not be started from this session (headless CLI authentication error); packet keyleaf/judge/BRIEF.txt + decode.txt frozen and ready. No read share or class claimed for pass 2 until it is scored.

Separate judge for pass 2 (keyleaf/judge/): model claude-opus-5-5, effort not exposed, session https://claude.ai/code/session_01P5UF3myhVjFtgU9vTMj1qn (an agent with its own context launched by the caller; same session as the solver, so separation stated, not shown), utc 2026-11-25T03:43:24Z; given only BRIEF.txt (sha256 af20815f) and decode.txt (41b28e8b). Strict letters S/(S+E+N), recomputed here from JUDGE_OUT.tsv: training f4r 600/703 = 85.35%, f4v 732/853 = 85.81% (training, not a test); H1 237/382 = 62.04% (under 65%, failed); H2 510/717 = 71.13%; H3 51/69 = 73.91% (pentacle 3 19/36 = 52.8% under 65%, failed; pentacle 4 32/33 = 97.0%); 62 pentacle rims 2221/2520 = 88.13%, 57 at or over 65%, under: S1-025 42.3%, S1-039 61.4%, S1-070 59.5%, S1-071 62.2%, S1-096 57.5%; all 4351/5244 = 82.97% (pool, not used). Swapped letter pairs scored N; line-end breaks without '=' not joined (joined 4377/5244 = 83.47%, no unit changes side). docs/_check_reading.py: every pass-2 section under the 0.45 clean-sentence bar (rims 23/62 = 0.371, H1 0/7, H2 0/11, H3 0/1 and 0/1), so 'read in part' wording is not allowed; each stays 'decoded, not read'. Proposed method for pass 2: read with known key for H2, H3 pentacle 4 and the 57 rims at or over 65%; the rest shown as failed. Not held out; no person has checked pass 2; first pass unchanged as figure of record.

Pass 3 (pass3/): f. 25r (canvas 53, page id 5353272) fetched at full size by plain GET from the e-manuscripta IIIF endpoint, HTTP 200 (pass3/BLOCKED.tsv: nothing blocked); the other images (ff. 15r, 52r-53r, key leaf f. 99r) were those fetched in pass 2. Split written before the fetch (pass3/SPLIT_P3.md, 07:44 UTC): H1r = f. 15r lines 1-12 re-read, declared not held out and not blind; H4 = f. 25r lines 1-12, never transcribed or decoded before, clear copy not to be looked for before the decode.

Key v3 (pass3/KEY_V3.tsv, pass3/RULES_V3.md): the 73 token values, 5 pairs and 2 word forms of keyleaf/KEY_LEAF.tsv re-checked against the leaf image f. 99r, no value changed (73 of 73 the same, pass3/checks/VERIFY_OUT.txt; 69 shapes exact, 4 probable). Decoder rules changed in five declared places before the freeze: C1 mark order (Tk^@ = rum, a pass-2 fault); C2 a nasal dot on a vowel + consonant group sign goes after the vowel (leaf wording and training leaf f. 4r); C3 two-dot fallback widened; C4 Cl Tq = rte and C5 x = ch in the chi-rho-iota abbreviation, both NOT on the key leaf.

Pass 3 transcriptions by Claude Fable 5.2 from full-size images, the reader knowing the key leaf (not shape-blind): H1 re-read (pass3/tx/f015r_p3.txt; 30 of 80 word groups differ from pass 2's keyleaf/tx2/f015r.txt; the reader had seen the clear copy f. 109v, so not blind), H4 f. 25r lines 1-12 (pass3/tx/f025r_H4.txt, 5 signs left ?), rims of second-series pentacles nos. 2-12, ff. 52r-53r, from own polar unwraps (pass3/tx/PENT_S2.txt). Doubts written before the freeze (pass3/DOUBTS_P3.md). Not transcribed: the figures on f. 54r, f. 97r-v, the texts inside the circles.

Freeze pass3/FREEZE_P3.txt 07:55:17 UTC: md5 and sha256 of the key, rules, decoder, three transcriptions, doubts, split and the f. 25r image. Unlike pass 2, this freeze was NOT time-stamped or pushed before the decode; its order rests on the run record and the hashes. The nine hashes were re-checked at 08:07 UTC and match.

One decode with key v3 (pass3/scripts/run_decode.py, 07:55:25 UTC; pass3/DECODE_P3.txt), no emendation (pass3/EMENDATIONS.md): H1r 405 letters, 0 signs with no value; H4 415 letters, 5 signs with no value; 11 rims 521 letters, 0 signs with no value. Not read under README Conventions: docs/_check_reading.py was not run on pass 3.

Solver's own strict count, not a separate judge (pass3/SCORE_P3.tsv): H1r 394/405 = 97.28%, H4 379/415 = 91.33%, rims 468/521 = 89.83% (S2-05 4/17 = 23.5%, under). H1r against the clear copy f. 109v: 399 of 425 clear letters matched = 93.9%. H4 not compared with its clear copy.

Shuffle control for pass 3 (pass3/scripts/control_p3.py, pass3/CONTROL_P3.txt): the 73 token values permuted, 5,000 keys at seeds 20261112 and 7, own Latin letter 4-gram model on la-latlib-letters.txt, log10 probability per character: H1r, H4, the rims as a section and each of the 11 rims 0/5000 at both seeds; z 11.7 / 11.7 (H1r), 9.8 / 9.8 (H4), 12.6 / 12.6 (rims), lowest single rim S2-05 z 4.6 / 4.5.

Prior-art look for the rim formulas (pass3/PRIOR_ART_P3.md): two web searches found no page with the Basel wording and no mention of a Basel cipher copy; genre parallel only (BL Stowe MS 16 ff. 151r-152r, amulet seals with Hoc signum captions, from Drieshen's BL blog post of 18 Jul 2019 read in a reprint). Not compared with the printed Key of Solomon legends (Mathers 1889; Skinner and Rankine 2008).

Separate judge for pass 3 (pass3/JUDGE_P3_RESULT.md, file time 08:05 UTC), launched by the calling session and given only pass3/judge/BRIEF.txt and pass3/judge/decode.txt; model and session not recorded in its file; the brief was written at 08:03 UTC, after the decode; separation stated, not shown. Strict letters S/(S+E+N), central call: H1r (re-read, NOT held out) 399/405 = 98.5% (range 97.3% to 98.8%); H4 (held out) 389/415 = 93.7% (range 93.0% to 95.9%); 11 second-series rims 486/521 = 93.3% (range 91.9% to 96.0%), 10 rims over 65%, S2-05 4/17 = 23.5% under, failed. The stretch H4 L09-L10 does not read. No pooled figure. The first pass stays the figure of record; no person has checked pass 3.

Variant without decoder rules C4 and C5 (neither is on the key leaf), declared at 08:07:22 UTC after the decode and the judging, then run on the same frozen key and transcriptions (pass3/variant/): H1r christiana -> iristiana, parte -> pa[?]te, ch~ri -> i~ri five times; S2-02 ch~ri -> i~ri; H4 unchanged letter for letter. Unchanged words keep the judge's central call; changed words called by the assembling session, not the judge: H1r 378/398 = 95.0% (every changed word N: 364/398 = 91.5%); H4 389/415 = 93.7%; rims 484/520 = 93.1% (strict 482/520 = 92.7%). H1r against the clear copy without C4 and C5: 386/425 = 90.8%. No unit changes side of the 65% line.

Time-stamp of the pass 3 working folder (pass3/stamps/, label basel-p3-25Nov): manifest of 37 files, sha256 4836e731..., RFC 3161 Sectigo and FreeTSA both granted 08:08:04 UTC on the first try, OpenTimestamps submitted and pending. The stamp is later than the decode and the judging.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was recovered from cipher ff. 4r-4v aligned word by word with the volume's own clear copy (ff. 101r-102r), frozen, and then used for one decode of three held-out passages (a strict judge finds 747 of 1,138 letters in words that read as sense; the decode reproduces 80.3% of the clear copy's letters); the volume's key leaf f. 99r, viewed only afterwards, agrees on 46 of 52 values. The decode does not yet read as sentences.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.md, counted with research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.measure_text over the three held-out passages: 113 of 225 decoded words read as sense (H1 35/77 = 0.455, H2 70/133 = 0.526, H3 8/15 = 0.533); one-letter slips (word(?)), no-sense words ([?word]) and signs with no key value ([?]) are holes. Strict judge by letters: 747/1,138 = 0.656 (judge/judge.tsv). The rest of the volume's cipher is not transcribed.

texts.label: H1: f. 15r, lines 1-12, conjurations (held out)
texts.summary: The end of one conjuration and the beginning of the next ('Alia coniuratio') in the Clavicula Salomonis: the spirits are adjured by the teachings of the faith, the saints, and the life of Christ (the Annunciation, the coming, the Nativity, the circumcision, the baptism, the fast, the Transfiguration on Mount Tabor). The volume's clear copy has the passage on f. 109v.
texts.note: Strict judge 229/367 letters = 62.4%, below the contributor's own 65% line; 35 of 77 words read as sense; no clean sentence.

texts.label: H2: f. 159r, Sigillum Iovis (held out)
texts.summary: The instructions for the seal of Jupiter in the Septem sigilla planetarum: cast in English tin on a day of Jupiter when the Moon enters Libra, with the planet's figure on one face and a priest-philosopher with a book on the other, and kept in sky-blue silk; carried, it wins love, grace and favour, increases fortune and frees its bearer from fear. Contents from the decode and the volume's clear copy (f. 167r).
texts.note: Strict judge 470/702 letters = 67.0%; 70 of 133 words read as sense; no clean sentence (0 of 11).

texts.label: H3: f. 34r, rims of pentacles 3 and 4 (held out)
texts.summary: The rim inscriptions of two pentacles: the bearer will fear neither the devil nor phantoms, and will not perish in arms. Contents from the volume's clear copy (f. 123r); the decode has a hole where 'non' stands in pentacle 4.
texts.note: Strict judge 48/69 letters = 69.6%; 8 of 15 words read as sense; no clean sentence (0 of 2).

outcome.notes: Held-out design: the key was built from ff. 4r-4v against the clear copy only; ff. 15r, 159r and 34r were decoded once with the frozen key, scored by a separate strict judge and, after the decode, against the clear copy. Blindness limits (FREEZE_TX.txt): the training leaves were transcribed with the clear copy beside them; the held-out leaves were transcribed by a reader who knew most of the system; the first two lines of H2's clear page were seen at contact-sheet size before the decode. The key leaf was viewed only after the key freeze and the decode (the contributor's record; the file times agree, and the RFC 3161 stamps of 21:21 UTC come after all of it). Class 'not read': the decode puts 65.6% of letters in words that read as sense but builds no clean sentence, so each passage is 'decoded, not read' under README Conventions ('A reading must read'); the contributor's working class was 'read in part'. Verification is of the key: the volume's clear copy (80.3% of its letters reproduced on the held-out passages) and its key leaf (46 of 52 values). The shuffle control and the judge are model work and are in the solution steps.
